scope: Prepared physical HW-FR test packages under docs/FULL-TEST-RELEASE.md (no authorization for physical operations is implied). No protocol has been executed on physical hardware. A protocol may only be run when its status is ready; every protocol is currently blocked for the reasons listed. tools/hw_evidence.py --check validates this file and every docs/verification/<new-directory>/hw-evidence*.json record.

signing.record_location: docs/verification/<new-directory>/hw-evidence*.json with the inventory and serial log in the same directory
signing.sign: ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <owner-private-key> -n baryonos-hw-evidence <record>  (produces <record>.sig; the private key never enters the repository)

forbidden_action_catalogue.no-firmware-flash: Do not flash, update or downgrade any firmware: UEFI/BIOS, embedded controller, management engine, option ROMs or peripheral firmware.
forbidden_action_catalogue.no-firmware-settings-save: Do not save any change in firmware setup. Setup may be opened read-only to record the Secure Boot state and must be left through 'discard changes and exit'.
forbidden_action_catalogue.no-bootorder-change: Do not create, delete or reorder UEFI boot entries and do not change BootOrder, BootNext or any other persistent UEFI variable. Boot only through the firmware one-time boot menu.
forbidden_action_catalogue.removable-media-only: Boot only the designated removable medium carrying the image whose SHA-256 is recorded; no network boot and no boot of the test image from an internal disk.
forbidden_action_catalogue.no-internal-disk-access: Internal disks are physically disconnected, or left in place untouched: no partitioning, formatting, mounting, reading of personal data or writing.
forbidden_action_catalogue.no-secure-boot-key-change: Do not change the Secure Boot state and do not enrol, replace or delete Secure Boot keys (PK, KEK, db, dbx, MOK).
forbidden_action_catalogue.no-personal-data: Attach no personal disk, account, real NAS content or personal storage peripheral; only the test medium and the listed test peripherals.
forbidden_action_catalogue.isolated-test-network: Connect the network port only to an isolated test switch or a dedicated test peer; no personal LAN, router or Internet uplink without a separate owner decision.
forbidden_action_catalogue.disposable-install-target-only: Install or recover only onto a second, designated disposable removable medium; never onto an internal disk.
forbidden_action_catalogue.no-unattended-sleep: Do not leave the machine unattended while it sleeps; when resume does not complete within the step time limit, end the session through the recovery route.

inventory_format.file: JSON object in the record directory, bound by inventory.sha256 in the signed record
inventory_format.keys: schema=2, kind='baryonos-hw-inventory', cpuid={vendor: 12-character CPUID vendor string, hypervisor_bit: CPUID.1:ECX[31] as boolean}, secure_boot='enabled'|'disabled'|'unknown', acpi={dmar: 'present'|'absent' (an ACPI DMAR table was found), drhd_units: integer 0..64, 0 when absent}, pci=[{address: 'ssss:bb:dd.f', vendor, device: 4 lowercase hex digits, class, subclass, prog_if, revision: 2 lowercase hex digits}]
inventory_format.dmar: acpi.dmar records only that the firmware publishes a DMAR table with the given number of DRHD units (read-only table observation). It is never evidence of VT-d containment; only a run's own *:BUS_MASTER:CONTAINED marker is. Schema-1 inventories are rejected.
inventory_format.rejection: A recorded hypervisor bit, or any PCI vendor 1af4 (virtio), 1b36 (QEMU), 1234 (QEMU/Bochs display), 15ad (VMware) or 80ee (VirtualBox), marks a virtual capture and the record is rejected.

protocols.title: Read-only native hardware inventory of the reference PC
blocking_reasons: The native-hw-inventory kernel profile does not exist (planned slice H06-T3); no code emits HWINV markers. The COM1 UNSUPPORTED:PCI inventory described in earlier documentation was never implemented.

No physical boot image exists: tools/build.py exports an ESP directory for QEMU's virtual FAT backend and tools/repro_check.py compares only that ESP payload manifest, so there is no removable-media image or image SHA-256 to bind.

Every milestone-m2 terminal path calls exit() in kernel/src/serial.rs, which writes QEMU's isa-debug-exit port 0xF4; that port is undefined on physical PCs, so a physical image first needs a halt-based terminal path.
The HW-FR target is null and docs/drivers/hw-allowed-signers lists no signer (owner decisions OD-HW-TARGETS and OD-HW-SIGNERS).
The output capture route is undecided (OD-HW-CAPTURE): COM1 output needs a physical serial port and a cable to a second computer; on-screen output of the markers is not demonstrated.
preconditions: Owner decisions OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-BOOT, OD-HW-DISKS, OD-HW-CAPTURE, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-PUBLISH and OD-HW-INV-ROUTE are recorded as decided.
The image is built from a clean checkout of the recorded source commit; the image SHA-256 and the source fingerprint v3 (source_hash in tools/common.py) are recorded before the session.
The removable medium contains only the verified image.
The machine is powered off and on mains power; internal disks are disconnected or untouched according to OD-HW-DISKS.
The capture route is connected and tested with the second computer before power-on.

steps.action: Open firmware setup read-only, record the Secure Boot state, leave through 'discard changes and exit'; re-read the image SHA-256 from the removable medium and compare it with the recorded value.
steps.expect: Secure Boot state recorded; hashes equal. If Secure Boot is enabled the unsigned image is expected to be refused: record the step as fail and stop.

steps.action: Start capture on the second computer (COM1 at 115200 8N1 through a null-modem cable, or the decided on-screen route) and record the capture command.
steps.expect: Capture running.

steps.action: Insert the removable medium, power on and select it once in the firmware one-time boot menu.
steps.expect: Firmware starts the removable medium without any persistent setting change.

steps.action: Wait at most 120 s for HWINV:PASS or a failure marker.
steps.expect: All required markers in order and no failure marker.

steps.action: Hold the power button at least 10 s until the machine is off; remove the medium; reconnect internal disks if they were disconnected; power on normally.
steps.expect: The previously installed system starts unchanged.

steps.action: Convert the HWINV lines into the inventory JSON, compute the SHA-256 of serial log and inventory, write the record in a new docs/verification child directory and sign it.
steps.expect: tools/hw_evidence.py --check accepts the record.

recovery_route: If no expected marker appears within the step time limit, the screen stays dark or the machine reboots: hold the power button at least 10 s until the machine is off.
Remove the removable medium and any test peripheral.

Reconnect internal disks only if they were disconnected for the session, then power on normally; the previous system starts unchanged because no firmware setting, boot entry or internal disk was changed.
If the previous boot behaviour does not return, stop: no firmware repair, CMOS clearing or reflashing; record the observation and escalate to the project owner.

protocols.title: Native ACPI S5 power-off by the independent kernel
blocking_reasons: No physical boot image exists: tools/build.py exports an ESP directory for QEMU's virtual FAT backend and tools/repro_check.py compares only that ESP payload manifest.

The UNAVAILABLE, UNREADABLE and REJECTED paths end through exit() in kernel/src/serial.rs, which writes QEMU's isa-debug-exit port 0xF4; that port is undefined on physical PCs, so the physical image needs a halt-based terminal path.

ACPI mode enable through SMI_CMD/ACPI_ENABLE is not implemented; the path assumes firmware already set SCI_EN=1, verified only on q35/OVMF. _PTS/_TTS are not executed; only the _S5_ package subset is parsed.
The HW-FR target, signer and capture route are undecided (OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-CAPTURE).

protocols.title: Native ACPI S3 sleep and wake by the independent kernel
blocking_reasons: Only a QEMU-native S3 path exists (kernel feature native-acpi-s3, docs/verification/h05-native-s3-20261119): its wake source is QMP system_wakeup, and on QEMU 8.2 + OVMF it arms a 32-bit extended waking vector under the QEMU/OVMF-specific Edk2Version0Extended policy (ADR-H05-S3-WAKE-20261119). The physical firmware path (FACS version, real-mode or extended vector, _PTS/_WAK needs) is unverified, and QEMU evidence is not physical evidence.
A physical wake needs an owner-decided wake source (power button, RTC alarm through the ACPI fixed RTC event, or a keyboard/USB wake with _PRW/GPE setup); none is implemented (OD-HW-POWER).
Completion must not rely on QEMU's isa-debug-exit port 0xF4, which is undefined on physical PCs; the post-resume terminal path must be a serial marker followed by a halt or by the validated S5 path.
No physical boot image exists, and the HW-FR target, signer and capture route are undecided (OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-CAPTURE).
preconditions: Owner decisions OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-BOOT, OD-HW-DISKS, OD-HW-CAPTURE, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-PUBLISH and OD-HW-POWER are recorded as decided, including the wake source.
Accepted HW-INV and H05-S5 records exist for the same target and source.
The image is built with the native-acpi-s3 kernel feature from a clean checkout of the recorded source commit; image SHA-256 and source fingerprint v3 are recorded.
The machine is powered off and on mains power; internal disks are disconnected or untouched according to OD-HW-DISKS.

protocols.title: USB keyboard and mouse through the native xHCI and USB-HID boot path
blocking_reasons: kernel/src/m2/xhci.rs accepts only QEMU's qemu-xhci controller (PCI 1b36:000d) at the fixed fixture MMIO address 0x3f210000; any physical xHCI controller is rejected before enumeration.
Bus mastering is enabled only inside an established native VT-d domain; the DMAR/VT-d availability of the physical target is unknown until HW-INV has run.
No interrupt, hub, general hotplug or reattach support exists; the expected input sequence is currently driven by QEMU QMP injection in tools/run_usb_hid.py.
The terminal path writes QEMU's isa-debug-exit port 0xF4, which is undefined on physical PCs.
No physical boot image exists, and the HW-FR target, signer and capture route are undecided (OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-CAPTURE).
preconditions: Owner decisions OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-BOOT, OD-HW-DISKS, OD-HW-CAPTURE, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-PUBLISH and OD-HW-FAMILIES are recorded as decided, including the named USB keyboard and mouse models.

An accepted HW-INV record for the same target, source and inventory exists; the bound inventory lists an xHCI function (PCI class 0c/03/30) and acpi.dmar='present' with drhd_units >= 1. DMAR presence is a table observation only and never evidence of VT-d containment, which only the USB:DOMAIN:PASS and USB:BUS_MASTER:CONTAINED markers of this run provide.
The image is built with the native-usb-hid-probe kernel feature from a clean checkout of the recorded source commit; image SHA-256 and source fingerprint v3 are recorded.
A USB boot-protocol keyboard and mouse are attached directly to root ports of the xHCI controller (no hub); internal disks are disconnected or untouched according to OD-HW-DISKS.

protocols.title: Installation onto and recovery from a disposable removable target
blocking_reasons: No installer or recovery image exists, and no NVMe, AHCI or USB mass-storage class driver exists to write a target medium.

Physical disk writes, firmware changes and boot-configuration changes on the physical device are not authorised (docs/FULL-TEST-RELEASE.md); this protocol therefore permits only a second disposable removable target, and internal-disk installation remains out of scope.
The terminal path writes QEMU's isa-debug-exit port 0xF4, which is undefined on physical PCs.

The install-target transport is undecided (OD-HW-DISKS, OD-HW-FAMILIES): USB mass storage, a removable SATA/eSATA bay (AHCI) or an external NVMe enclosure. A run may list nvme or ahci only when the serial log carries that controller's own INSTALL:TARGET:NVME:* or INSTALL:TARGET:AHCI:* marker; an install to a USB or other removable target lists no storage device and proves only the install procedure.
The HW-FR target, signer and capture route are undecided (OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-CAPTURE).
preconditions: Owner decisions OD-HW-TARGETS, OD-HW-BOOT, OD-HW-DISKS, OD-HW-CAPTURE, OD-HW-SIGNERS, OD-HW-PUBLISH and OD-HW-FAMILIES are recorded as decided, including a written authorization for writes to the named disposable target medium and the install-target transport.
Accepted HW-INV, H02-USB and H05-S5 records exist for the same target and source.
The installer image is built from a clean checkout of the recorded source commit; image SHA-256 and source fingerprint v3 are recorded.
A second, empty, labelled disposable removable medium is the only writable target; internal disks are disconnected or untouched according to OD-HW-DISKS.
